newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia accounting rule change creates quandary.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia accounting rule change creates quandary.

text.p: A set of new guidelines from the Malaysian Institute of Accountants has created a quandary for corporations, as the changes could allow two companies involved in an acquisition to count the same profit twice, the Asian Wall Street Journal said on Friday.

For example, the daily pointed to Sime Darby Bhd's mid-November signing of an agreement to buy a 60 percent stake in United Malayan Banking Corp (UMBC) from Datuk Keramat Holdings Bhd for 1.3 billion ringgit.
Executives familiar with the situation say that Sime Darby's consolidated results for the year ended June 30 -- set to be released on Saturday -- will include the earnings of UMBC, the article said.

But Datuk Keramat has also consolidated UMBC's earnings for part of the same period in its own results for the year ended January 30 on the grounds that it only handed over its stake in the banking group to Sime Darby in April, after all conditions of the sale agreement were met.

The quandary arises from a new set of guidelines issued last month by the Malaysian Institute of Accountants, the profession's chief governing body, on the treatment of income derived from acquisitions by corporate entities when they consolidate their accounts at the group level.

For years, the institute said that income from acquired assets can only be recognised in the purchaser's accounts after the purchase is completed. But accountants say a set of supplementary guidelines paved the way for purchasers to consolidate earnings from the date a purchase agreement is signed, the newspaper said.
A Sime Darby spokesman did not immediately have a comment on Friday when contacted by Reuters.
A survey of 31 stockbroking houses showed a forecast net profit of 611.3 million ringgit or 28.4 cents a share for Sime's 1996 results, Reuters previously reported.

Analysts previously told Reuters they expected earnings to be at the lower end of the forecast range due to smaller contribution from UMBC, since the acquisition was completed in April this year, later than expected.
